newsitem.title: UK: British submariners risk trauma death - study.
newsitem.headline: British submariners risk trauma death - study.

text.p: Britain's submariners suffer unusually low rates of cancer, despite their exposure to nuclear-powered engines -- but they tend to die more from alcohol abuse or accidents, researchers said on Thursday.

As well as having low rates of cancer, Sailors assigned to submarines have low rates of respiratory disease, but this could be because only the healthiest recruits go onto submarines, Dr Hazel Inskip of the University of Southampton said.
Inskip looked at the records of 15,000 submariners and found to her surprise that they had high rates of death from suicide and accidents such as drowning, as well as from cirrhosis of the liver.

"Risk-taking may have increased when people were freed from the discipline of the services and, as with cirrhosis, alcohol may have played part," she wrote in a report in the journal of Occupational and Environmental Medicine.
The report was commissioned by the Ministry of Defence, which was concerned about the possible effect of radiation on sailors serving aboard nuclear submarines.
